必需章节、会话清单及日志格式。\r\n包检查还会核对固件摘要、补丁格式和仓库卫生；这些检查不能替代全量许可证审查或实板验收。\r\n测试所需环境及换行符注意事项见[测试说明](app/espdl-quickapp/tests/README.md)。\r\n\r\n# ESP-DL 人脸跟随与物体分类\r\n\r\n同一固件中的 ESPClaw 触屏聊天、服务配置及共用 HTTPS 说明见 [CHAT.md](CHAT.md)。\r\n双网络使用有效有线网关优先、Wi-Fi 备用：网线只有链路但没有 DHCP 地址时，\r\n不抢占无线外网出口。桌面统一管理 `eth0` / `wlan0` 的 DHCP 和 DNS，\r\n构建必须关闭 `CONFIG_NSH_NETINIT`，避免 UDP 68 端口和 DNS 被两个初始化任务争用。\r\n插线后会申请有线租约，断线后 DNS 回到可用的 Wi-Fi；网口启停不直接操作 LVGL。\r\n内置录音机、GPIO／I²C／SPI／UART／PWM／舵机／音频／BLE 快应用接口与 AI 参考见 [HARDWARE.md](HARDWARE.md)。\r\nHome Assistant 原生米家页的实体范围、分页、状态色、控制确认和布局依据见\r\n[HA-TILE-DESIGN.md](HA-TILE-DESIGN.md)。\r\n\r\n大肥鱼桌宠 1.0.1 的原生浮层、`system.pet` API 和快应用源码已接入当前 overlay，\r\n说明与许可证见 [dafeiyu/README.md](overlay/apps/system/desktop/dafeiyu/README.md)。\r\n桌宠已通过宿主 C/JS 测试、固件构建和实板启动测试；`desktop ui pet` 可启动内置\r\nQuickJS 应用。固件优先加载 `/sdcard/dafeiyu/dafeiyu.lvbin` 中预转换的上游原版精灵，\r\n资源缺失或校验失败时回退到内置几何形象。单击、双击、拖拽及原版精灵显示仍须以\r\n当前固件对应的实板记录为准。\r\n\r\n面向 ESP32-P4 Function-EV-Board 的内置快应用，使用 USB MJPEG 相机和本地 ESP-DL 模型。仅提供两个模式：\r\n\r\n- **人脸跟随**：连续采集、MSR/MNP 两阶段人脸检测、跨帧几何关联、目标框和中心偏移提示。短暂丢失时不切到远处另一张脸，连续三次丢失后重新选取目标。当前是画面内跟踪；没有人脸身份注册/比对，也没有连接云台或舵机。\r\n- **物体分类**：拍摄一帧，使用 ImageNet MobileNetV2 显示前三个类别及分数。类别为模型自带英文名称。\r\n\r\nP4 神经网络加速使用 ESP-DL 官方 `xespv` 向量指令、`xesploop` 硬件循环及标量 FPU。NuttX 扩展上下文保存 Q0–Q7、QACC、UA、XACC、SAR、SAR_BYTES、FFT、CFG 和两个硬件循环的状态。异常帧强制 16 字节对齐并记录原始 SP，兼容算子内部暂时不对齐的栈；P4 非懒加载 FPU 路径在异常入口完整保存浮点寄存器与 FCSR。任务可被抢占；中断处理器不运行向量算子。尚未接入 PPA、硬件 JPEG 解码或双核并行算子。\r\n\r\n图像链路为 MJPEG 软件解码 → 标准 RGB565 → C 图像缩放/归一化 → P4 加速神经网络。修正了解码器红蓝通道颠倒，以及启用缩放时只缩小输出矩形、未缩小像素块的问题。`640×480 → 320×240` 现在对 MCU 像素块真正取平均；软件解码四种比例均与独立 libjpeg/Pillow 结果对比。\r\n\r\n帧率优化版对 JPEG 热点使用 `-O2`，缩放后尺寸匹配时直接解码到工作线程的目标帧，复用每个模型会话的归一化表与检测后处理对象。每帧完整执行 MSR/MNP；检测结果列表在重用前清空。移除慢帧结束后固定的 20 毫秒等待，快帧按 100 毫秒周期调度；界面每 50 毫秒检查新帧，只渲染匹配的图像与检测框。100 毫秒是目标周期，实际帧率以 `perf frames=30 wall=...` 计数为准。\r\n\r\n当前工具链是 Espressif GCC 14.2.0_20251107。SDK 根据 GCC 主版本判断广播加载指令步长不可靠，移植改用零步长加载加显式地址累加；`MALLOC_CAP_SIMD` 分配保证 16 字节对齐。实板逐像素对比仍发现 SDK 图像 SIMD helper 存在剩余差异（`evidence/face-simd-9.json`），因此生产预处理明确选用 C 实现；卷积、深度卷积、矩阵运算继续使用原始 P4 SIMD 权重及算子。\r\n\r\n源码固定到 ESP-DL v3.2.0、提交 `dc380d450835d42f92777121a0cd4fc67d7c3a8c`。模型包使用该提交原始 P4 权重布局，实际运行前检查每个文件的长度及 SHA-256。没有配置网络识别服务。\r\n\r\n## Flash 布局\r\n\r\n下述布局记录历史开发过程中对 `/data` 的迁移，不构成对当前设备再次擦除数据的授权。16 MiB flash 的布局如下，地址区间右端不包含在内：\r\n\r\n| 用途 | 起始地址 | 结束地址 |\r\n| --- | --- | --- |\r\n| Simple Boot 固件 | `0x2000` | 小于 `0x800000` |\r\n| 模型包 | `0x800000` | 小于 `0xc00000` |\r\n| SmartFS `/data` | `0xc00000` | `0x1000000` |\r\n\r\n程序通过 `CONFIG_ESPRESSIF_STORAGE_MTD_OFFSET=0xc00000` 访问新数据区，大小仍为 4 MiB。模型优先从 `/sdcard/espdl/` 按 manifest 文件名读取，否则访问 flash 模型区。请只安装 `models/manifest.json` 列出的三个模型；开发目录里可能保留早期实验产物。\r\n\r\n`diagnostics/flash_espdl.py` 默认只检查文件和显示写入范围，`--execute` 才烧录到已识别的 COM23 开发板。已有模型和 SmartFS 的开发板更新请使用 `--execute --firmware-only`，保留模型与 `/data`。首次完整烧录会清空新数据区，需要启动后运行 `mksmartfs /dev/smart0` 和 `mount -t smartfs /dev/smart0 /data`。回退旧固件需要同时重新处理旧 `/data` 所在区域。\r\n\r\n## 构建和验证\r\n\r\n当前脚本仍依赖 WSL 中已有相机基线 `/tmp/v3-desktop-camera-usb-20260914` 和已安装 Espressif 工具链。按顺序运行：\r\n\r\n1. `diagnostics/prepare_espdl_work.py`（WSL）\r\n2. `diagnostics/prepare_espdl_context.py`（WSL）\r\n3. `diagnostics/package_espdl_models.py`（Windows 或 WSL）\r\n4. `diagnostics/build_espdl_library.py`（WSL）\r\n5. `diagnostics/build_espdl.py`（WSL）\r\n\r\n隔离树为 `/tmp/v3-desktop-espdl-20260915`。完整固件使用 ILP32F ABI，C++、TLS 和全部系统对象必须匹配；不能把旧软浮点对象混入。\r\n\r\n主机测试：`diagnostics/test_espdl.py` 检查真实 C 跟踪/服务代码的内存与未定义行为、取消、断开、重复开始、帧一致性及 SHA-256，并检查实际 MJPEG 解码器四种缩放比例的越界、重复解码与截断输入。`diagnostics/inspect_espdl_pixels.py` 独立对比颜色及缩放像素；`node tests/test_app.js overlay/apps/system/desktop/espdl/app.js` 验证快应用切换和渲染时序。\r\n\r\n实板诊断：`desktop espdl test 0` 依次运行同核 FPU/向量抢占与重复 Gemm 自检、图像预处理对照、官方 320×240 人脸 JPEG 的两次完整推理、分类重复推理。终端等待工作线程结束再返回；`desktop espdl` 查询完成状态。自检中的图像 SIMD 差异是诊断记录，所选 C 预处理必须通过独立 RGB565 数值参考检查。`desktop ui espdl` 打开应用，`desktop ui espdl-start` 开始跟随，`desktop ui espdl-stop` 停止。UI 只从完整发布的同一帧读取图像和检测结果，工作线程不访问 LVGL。\r\n\r\n证据分别保存在 `evidence/firmware-validation.json`、`evidence/host-validation.json`、`evidence/js-validation.json` 和实板日志。构建或主机测试通过不能代替实板识别准确性、帧率和长期稳定性验证。\r\n## Local verified source release: 2026-09-19\r\n\r\nThe application source in this directory is synchronized from the locally verified 04-v3-20260913/espdl-quickapp tree. In each multi-series SVG, give the full-plot overlay both `data-chart-hit` and `data-chart-hover-overlay=\"cross-series\"`. Keep the `data-chart-hover-guide` at the exact cursor x, interpolate every visible series there, and show one aligned `data-chart-hover-marker` and tooltip row per visible series; never snap the guide to a nearby sample. Never add a KPI row, controls, cards, or panels unless those UI elements are explicitly requested.\r\n- For sequences or parallel work, use aligned lanes on one time axis. Render every requested dimension simultaneously; never hide one behind a toggle.\r\n\r\n### Maps\r\n\r\n- Let the map dominate the composition. Use at most one compact selection/detail area and only requested controls.\r\n- Always project published GeoJSON/TopoJSON and sourced longitude/latitude with `d3-geo`; never hard-code or hand-draw geographic outlines. Use schematic maps only when asked.\r\n- For world countries, import `https://esm.sh/@d3-maps/atlas@1.0.0/world/countries/countries-110m` and convert it with `topojson-client@3.1.0` using `feature(world, world.objects.features).features`. Allow only selection unless asked.\r\n\r\n### Part-to-whole or time allocation\r\n\r\n- Use compact metrics and one stacked chart of category allocation per period. Never substitute totals-only bars or duplicate it as a heatmap and totals chart.\r\n\r\n## Layout and accessibility\r\n\r\n- Use semantic HTML, keyboard-accessible controls, and concise labels.\r\n- Use `aria-live=\"polite\"` for dynamic results, selections, and simulator updates. Reflow by stacking or wrapping; use `.table-responsive` only when table columns cannot fit. The host sizes the frame to its content, so avoid fixed outer widths, other horizontal overflow, internal scrolling, `position: fixed`, and viewport-height layouts.\r\n- Size every SVG from its actual container. Use the matching utility for every button and form control. L204: # Grok Ball
L205: 
L206: 一个会「看」你的 AI 表情球：圆球 + 一双眼睛实时跟随鼠标，内置 32 种表情状态（生命周期 / 情绪反应 / 代理工作状态三组），纯 SVG 驱动、零运行依赖。
L207: 
L208: > 灵感来自 Grok 的 Logo 动态效果，但本项目与 xAI / Grok 无关，代码为原创实现。
L209: ## 特性
L210: 
L211:   * 单文件成品：`index.html` 内联压缩后的引擎，一个文件即可运行，无需 npm 或外部资源。
L212:   * 原始眼环几何：25 组左右各 48 点的轮廓，保留比例、位置与左右不对称细节。
L213:   * 真实球面投影：基于身体轮廓采样、经度换算和余弦压缩；自旋到背面时眼睛自动隐藏。
L214:   * 32 种表情：睡眠、待机、好奇、开心、惊讶、生气、思考中、任务完成、检索资料……全部可切换。
L215:   * 完整动画：逐点眼环形变、眨眼弹簧、注视、呼吸、序列动画、3D 彩带、睡眠 zzz、撒花。
L216:   * 可嵌入业务：提供 `GrokBall.create()` SDK，可用 `emotionId` 直接对接 AI 输出。
L217:   * 可维护源码：提供可直接引用的 JS 运行时和带 Agent 消息类型的 TypeScript 入口。
L218:   * MIT 协议：免费使用、修改、商用均可。
L219: 
L220: ## 在线效果预览

cmake_out/vela_goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/\r\n```\r\n\r\n**成功标志**: 出现 `goldfish-armv8a-ap>` NSH 提示符\r\n\r\n### 清理编译\r\n\r\n```bash\r\nrm -rf <OUTPUT_DIR>\r\n```\r\n\r\n全量清理后重新编译：\r\n```bash\r\nrm -rf /* Optional per-polygon pixel raster, for the isolated mini preview. */
static bool grok_mosaic_on_stroke(const struct qpk_polygon_s *p,int x,int y);
static uint32_t grok_mosaic_color(const struct qpk_polygon_s *p,int x,int y)
{
  if(!p->gradient.kind)return p->color;
  double half=p->pixel_cell*0.5;
  if(p->gradient.kind==1&&p->pixel_cell==1) {
    if(grok_mosaic_on_stroke(p,x,y))return 0x989b95;
    lv_color_t c=qpk_polygon_color(p,x+half,y+half);
    int brightness=(c.red+c.green+c.blue)/3;
    return brightness>244?0xf7f6f0:brightness>233?0xebe9e1:brightness>221?0xdddbd2:brightness>205?0xc8c7bd:0xb2b3ac;
  }
  lv_color_t c=qpk_polygon_color(p,x+half,y+half);
  /* Sixteen levels per channel, without dithering or edge antialiasing. */
  return (((c.red+8)/17*17)<<16)|(((c.green+8)/17*17)<<8)|((c.blue+8)/17*17);
}

# openvela Build

编译 openvela 固件、修改内核配置、运行模拟器。

## 默认目标

默认编译目标为 goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap（64 位 ARM 模拟器）：

```
CONFIG_PATH=vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/
OUTPUT_DIR=cmake_out/vela_goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/
```

如果用户指定了其他板级配置路径，替换上述路径即可。

## 命令

### 编译

```bash
./build.sh <CONFIG_PATH> --cmake -j$(nproc)
```

示例：
```bash
./build.sh vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/ --cmake -j$(nproc)
```

**成功标志**: 输出 `#### build completed successfully`

**编译产物**: `<OUTPUT_DIR>/nuttx`（ELF）、`<OUTPUT_DIR>/vela_ap.bin`

### 修改内核配置（menuconfig）

```bash
./build.sh <CONFIG_PATH> --cmake menuconfig
```

menuconfig 是交互式 TUI 界面，**不能在 AI 终端中直接运行**。提示用户在自己的终端中执行。

修改配置后保存会自动更新 `.config`。如需持久化到 defconfig：
```bash
./build.sh <CONFIG_PATH> --cmake savedefconfig
```

### 运行模拟器

```bash
./emulator.sh <OUTPUT_DIR>
```

示例：
```bash
./emulator.sh cmake_out/vela_goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/
```

**成功标志**: 出现 `goldfish-armv8a-ap>` NSH 提示符

### 清理编译

```bash
rm -rf <OUTPUT_DIR>
```

全量清理后重新编译：
```bash
rm -rf cmake_out/vela_goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/ && ./build.sh vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/ --cmake -j$(nproc)
```

## 编译流程

1. 用户指定或确认目标配置路径
2. 执行 `./build.sh <path> --cmake -j$(nproc)`
3. 检查输出最后几行是否包含 `build completed successfully`
4. 如果编译失败，分析错误日志并尝试修复（最多 3 轮）

## 编译失败处理

| 错误类型 | 特征 | 处理 |
|----------|------|------|
| 代码错误 | `error:` + 本驱动文件名 | 自动修复代码，重新编译 |
| 配置缺失 | `undefined reference` + CONFIG 相关 | 提示用户 menuconfig 开启 |
| 工具链问题 | `command not found` | 提示用户安装工具链 |
| 缓存问题 | 奇怪的链接错误 | `rm -rf <OUTPUT_DIR>` 后重编 |

## 启用新驱动的 CONFIG

如果需要临时启用某个 CONFIG 进行编译验证：

```bash
# 方法 1: 直接追加到 defconfig（推荐）
echo "CONFIG_SENSORS_BME680=y" >> <CONFIG_PATH>/defconfig

# 方法 2: 用 sed 修改 .config（临时，不持久化）
sed -i 's/# CONFIG_SENSORS_BME680 is not set/CONFIG_SENSORS_BME680=y/' <OUTPUT_DIR>/.config
```

修改后重新编译即可。

## 常用配置路径

| 目标 | 配置路径 |
|------|----------|
| goldfish-arm64 (推荐) | `vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/goldfish-arm64-v8a-ap/` |
| goldfish-arm32 | `vendor/openvela/boards/vela/configs/goldfish-armeabi-v7a-ap/` |
| 自定义板级 | `vendor/<vendor>/boards/<chip>/<board>/configs/<config>/` |

# Grok Ball / LVGL

OuO 入口现使用 [tycoding/grok-ball](https://github.com/tycoding/grok-ball) 的表情引擎。上游固定在 de368ce3acdc5a70e871ee46ebbe8f60b11d3d6a，原文件未改写，MIT 许可和来源哈希在 vendor/ 保留。LVGL 适配代码为 Apache-2.0。

保留上游 32 种表情、48 点眼睛轮廓、动画、注视、自旋彩带和 AI emotionId 接口。浏览器 SVG 场景映射到原生 LVGL 多边形，没有 WebView。填充按完整轮廓扫描，避免三角形拼接细线和缺口。渐变保留全部色标并由原生 LVGL 分段插值，字体和抗锯齿由 LVGL 绘制，因此不是浏览器逐像素复刻。

触摸球体时眼睛跟随，轻点自旋，左右滑动切换表情。底部“表情”打开生命周期、情绪反应、工作状态三个分组，可直接选中全部 32 种表情；还可启动/停止巡演或进入思考状态。面板打开时停止巡演并暂停背景动画，选择/关闭后恢复；背景按键不会穿透触发。表情使用本包 storage 保存，跨重启保存取决于数据文件系统。

原引擎的 active 开关已启用，自动眨眼、眼环池轮换、待机小动作及进入状态时的自旋/撒花均运行；动画仍由单个原生定时器驱动。AI tips 从事件的 text 字段读取，状态切换会清除旧提示。暂停同时停止巡演。

- vendor/grok-ball.js：固定版本的上游引擎。

- app.js、ouo_resource.c：由 python tools/generate_grok_ouo.py 生成，勿独立编辑。

生成器同步内置应用、ESPClaw 示例、清单和嵌入资源。保留原 OuO 包名、目录和 CLI 入口，显示名 Grok Ball，版本 2.0.0。状态 ID 改用上游定义，详见 DESIGN.md。

L42: Home Assistant extends the cite34†Jinja2 template engine†jinja.palletsprojects.com with many custom functions, filters, and tests. Each one has its own page with detailed descriptions, parameters, and practical examples.
L43:

L47: ### Areas
L48: 
L49: These template functions let you work with the areas you've set up in Home Assistant. Look up which entities or devices belong to an area, get area names and IDs, and build automations that operate on entire rooms at once.
L50:   * cite35†Get devices in an area `area_devices` Returns a list of device IDs associated with a given area.
L51:   * cite36†Get entities in an area `area_entities` Returns a list of entity IDs associated with a given area.
L52:   * cite37†Get area ID `area_id` Returns the area ID for a given area name, entity ID, or device ID.
L53:   * cite38†Get area name `area_name` Returns the friendly name of an area from its ID, entity ID, or device ID.
L54:   * cite39†Get all areas `areas` Returns a list of all area IDs in your Home Assistant instance.
L55: ### Collections
L56: 
L57: These template functions help you work with collections of data: lists, sets, dictionaries, and JSON. Use them to combine, filter, sort, and reshape data from your entities, API responses, and incoming messages.
L58:   * cite40†Get object attribute `attr` Reads an attribute from an object when the attribute name comes from a variable.
L59:   * cite41†Split list into batches `batch` Splits a list into smaller batches of a specified size.
L60:   * cite42†Merge dictionaries `combine` Merges multiple dictionaries into one.
L61:   * cite43†Sort a dictionary `dictsort` Sorts a dictionary by its keys or values, returning a list of key/value pairs.
L62:   * cite44†Set difference `difference` Returns items in the first list but not in the second (set difference).
L63:   * cite45†Get first item `first` Returns the first item of a list or the first character of a string.
L64:   * cite46†Flatten nested lists `flatten` Flattens nested lists into a single flat list.
L65:   * cite47†Parse JSON string `from_json` Parses a JSON string into a Python object.
L66:   * cite48†Group items by attribute `groupby` Groups a list of items by a common attribute, producing a list of (grouper, list) pairs.
L67:   * cite49†Set intersection `intersect` Returns items common to both lists (set intersection).
L68:   * cite50†Get dictionary key/value pairs `items` Returns the key/value pairs from a dictionary as a list of tuples.
L69:   * cite51†Get last item `last` Returns the last item of a list or the last character of a string.
L70:   * cite52†Get length of a collection `length` Returns the number of items in a list, characters in a string, or keys in a dictionary. Also available as count.
L71:   * cite53†Transform list items `map` Applies a filter to each item or extracts an attribute from each item in a list.
L72:   * cite54†Merge action responses `merge_response` Merges action response dictionaries into a flat list.
L73:   * cite55†Remove items by test `reject` Filters a list, removing items that pass a given test. The opposite of select.
L74:   * cite56†Remove items by attribute test `rejectattr` Filters a list, removing items where a specified attribute passes a test. The opposite of selectattr.
L75:   * cite57†Reverse a list or string `reverse` Reverses the order of items in a list or characters in a string.
L76:   * cite58†Filter items by test `select` Filters a list, keeping only items that pass a given test.
L77:   * cite59†Filter items by attribute test `selectattr` Filters a list, keeping only items where a specified attribute passes a test.
L78:   * cite60†Convert to set `set` Converts an iterable to a set, removing duplicate values.
L79:   * cite61†Randomly shuffle a list `shuffle` Randomly shuffles the items in a list.
L80:   * cite62†Slice a list into sub-lists `slice` Slices a list into a specified number of sub-lists of roughly equal size.
L81:   * cite63†Sort a list `sort` Sorts the items in a list, with optional attribute-based and reverse sorting.
L82:   * cite64†Sum values in a list `sum` Sums all values in a list, with optional attribute extraction and start value.
L83:   * cite65†Set symmetric difference `symmetric_difference` Returns items in either list but not in both.
L84:   * cite66†Serialize to JSON `to_json` Serializes a value to a JSON string.
L85:   * cite67†Convert to tuple `tuple` Converts an iterable to a tuple.
L86:   * cite68†Set union `union` Returns all unique items from both lists (set union).
L87:   * cite69†Remove duplicate values `unique` Removes duplicate values from a list, keeping only unique items.
L88: ### Comparison
L89: 
L90: These template tests let you compare values in your templates. Use them inside if conditions and filters to check equality, order, or membership.
L91:   * cite70†Test equality `eq` Tests if two values are equal. Also known as equalto or ==.
L92:   * cite71†Test greater than or equal `ge` Tests if a value is greater than or equal to another. Also known as >=.
L93:   * cite72†Test greater than `gt` Tests if a value is greater than another. Also known as greaterthan or >.
L94:   * cite73†Test less than or equal `le` Tests if a value is less than or equal to another. Also known as <=.
L95:   * cite74†Test less than `lt` Tests if a value is less than another. Also known as lessthan or <.
L96:   * cite75†Test not equal `ne` Tests if two values are not equal. Also known as !=.
L97: ### Date & Time
L98: 
L99: These template functions help you work with dates, times, and durations. Use them to get the current time, format timestamps for display, calculate how long ago something happened, or convert between different time representations.
L100:   * cite76†Convert to datetime `as_datetime` Converts a string or timestamp to a datetime object.
L101:   * cite77†Convert to local time zone `as_local` Converts a datetime object to your local time zone.
L102:   * cite78†Parse duration string `as_timedelta` Parses an ISO 8601 duration string into a timedelta object.
L103:   * cite79†Convert to UNIX timestamp `as_timestamp` Converts a datetime object or string to a UNIX timestamp.
L104:   * cite80†Current local date and time `now` Returns the current date and time in your local time zone.
L105:   * cite81†Relative time (deprecated) `relative_time` Returns a human-readable string describing how long ago a datetime was.
L106:   * cite82†Parse a time string `strptime` Parses a time string with a specified format into a datetime object.
L107:   * cite83†Human-readable time elapsed `time_since` Returns a human-readable string describing how much time has passed since a datetime.
L108:   * cite84†Human-readable time remaining `time_until` Returns a human-readable string describing how much time remains until a datetime.
L109:   * cite85†Create a time duration `timedelta` Creates a timedelta object from numeric time components.
L110:   * cite86†Human-readable duration `timedelta_string` Returns a human-readable string representation of a timedelta duration.
L111:   * cite87†Format timestamp with custom format `timestamp_custom` Formats a UNIX timestamp as a string using a custom format.
L112:   * cite88†Format timestamp as local time `timestamp_local` Formats a UNIX timestamp as a local datetime string.
L113:   * cite89†Format timestamp as UTC time `timestamp_utc` Formats a UNIX timestamp as a UTC datetime string.
L114:   * cite90†Today at a specific time `today_at` Returns today's date combined with a specific time.
L115:   * cite91†Current UTC date and time `utcnow` Returns the current date and time in UTC.
L116: ### Devices
L117:

L119:   * cite92†Get device attribute `device_attr` Returns the value of a specific attribute from a device.

L125: 
L126: These template functions encode, decode, and hash data. Use them to turn bytes into readable text, generate checksums, or prepare data for APIs that expect a specific encoding.
L127:   * cite97†Decode from base64 `base64_decode` Decodes a base64-encoded string.
L128:   * cite98†Encode to base64 `base64_encode` Encodes a string or bytes to a base64 string.
L129:   * cite99†Decode hex string to bytes `from_hex` Decodes a hexadecimal string into bytes.
L130:   * cite100†MD5 hash `md5` Calculates the MD5 hash of a string.
L131:   * cite101†Pack value to bytes `pack` Packs a value into bytes using a Python struct format string.
L132:   * cite102†SHA1 hash `sha1` Calculates the SHA1 hash of a string.
L133:   * cite103†SHA256 hash `sha256` Calculates the SHA256 hash of a string.
L134:   * cite104†SHA512 hash `sha512` Calculates the SHA512 hash of a string.
L135:   * cite105†Unpack bytes to value `unpack` Unpacks bytes into a value using a Python struct format string.
L136: ### Entities
L137:

L139:   * cite106†Get config entry attribute `config_entry_attr` Gets a specific attribute from a config entry.
L140:   * cite107†Get config entry ID `config_entry_id` Gets the config entry ID from an entity ID.

L142:   * cite109†Get entities for an integration `integration_entities` Returns a list of entity IDs tied to an integration or config entry.

L145:

L169: ### Labels
L170:

点击小卡仍可打开网页快捷卡片；首页大卡直接展示同样的快捷控制。“更多操作”进入统一后的原有详情与亮度调整，从首页大卡进入时返回原组合，从展开卡片进入时返回该快捷卡片。

# Contest Log Collector — openvela AI 大赛 AI Coding 日志归集

为 openvela AI 大赛提供 AI Coding 日志归集能力,**工作区感应、对话结束自动入仓**。

## 核心架构

```
       ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
       │ 门控: 当前目录向上能找到 .repo/ ?                    │
       │   否 → 不在 openvela 工作区 → 完全不采集             │
       │   是 → 在 openvela 工作区 → 进入采集                 │
       └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                               │ (在工作区内)
                               ↓
       ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
       │ 对话结束自动写入: demo 仓 logs/<login>/              │
       │ 只写文件,不自动 commit/push                         │
       │ 选手 git push 时跟代码一起上 GitHub                  │
       └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**关键安全特性**: 用"是否在 openvela 工作区(`.repo/`)内"作为隐私门控 —— 选手在个人项目(工作区外)跟 AI 聊的对话**完全不采集**;只有在比赛工作区内的对话才会自动写入选手仓 `logs/`,且工具自身**永远不会 git push**,上传由选手控制。

## 自动入仓(默认,无需操作)

在 openvela 工作区内跟 AI 工具(Claude Code / OpenCode / Codex)对话,会话结束时日志会**自动写入**选手仓的 `logs/<github_login>/`。选手只需在提交代码时一起 push:

```bash
git add logs/
git commit -s -m "logs: capture session"
git push
```

## (可选)手动补导

正常流程不需要,但你可以用手动工具查看清单或补导某次会话。

### 1. 短命令 `contest-snapshot`(`install.sh` 装在 `~/.local/bin/`)

```bash
# 列出本机已采集的所有 session
contest-snapshot --list

# 补导某个 session (加 --confirm 真写入)
contest-snapshot --session <session-id> --confirm

# 按日期补导
contest-snapshot --today --confirm
contest-snapshot --since 2026-06-15 --confirm
```

### 2. 完整路径 fallback(`~/.local/bin` 不在 PATH 时)

```bash
python3 ../.claude/skills/contest-log-collector/tools/export-session.py --list
```

### 3. 自然语言 / Slash command

对 AI 说"补导这次会话",或在 Claude Code 里跑 `/contest-snapshot`,AI 会调用 `export-session.py` 预览,确认后加 `--confirm` 写入。

> ⚠️ 手动工具的 `--confirm`:不加时只预览不写文件。手动补导仅用于补救/管理,正常对话已自动入仓。

Render one real `<button type=\"button\" aria-pressed=\"true\">` per series with a small swatch and neutral text; toggle its line, markers, and tooltip row together. Keep buttons transparent, borderless, and indistinguishable from inline text; never use `.btn`, pills, badges, rounded borders, or filled and selected backgrounds.\r\n- Share one root-relative, pointer-transparent `<div class=\"tooltip\" role=\"tooltip\">` using `--popover` and `--popover-foreground`. In each multi-series SVG, give the full-plot overlay both `data-chart-hit` and `data-chart-hover-overlay=\"cross-series\"`. Keep the `data-chart-hover-guide` at the exact cursor x, interpolate every visible series there, and show one aligned `data-chart-hover-marker` and tooltip row per visible series; never snap the guide to a nearby sample. Let touch users pin the same cross-series details without requiring hover.\r\n- Find ordered observations with `d3.bisector(d => d.x).center(values, x)`; never pass an accessor to `d3.bisectCenter`.\r\n- Give isolated marks transparent `data-chart-hit` targets at least 32 screen pixels across on fine pointers and about 44px on coarse pointers; use one nearest-point overlay for dense scatter.\r\n- For named numeric data and one-off analyses, start with the plot. Put values and takeaways on its marks, axes, or annotations. Never add a KPI row, controls, cards, or panels unless those UI elements are explicitly requested.\r\n- For sequences or parallel work, use aligned lanes on one time axis. Encode phase and resource in the marks; annotate totals, waits, and bottlenecks on the axis or lanes, not above the plot.\r\n- For distributions or multi-metric comparisons, use shared-scale facets or small multiples. Render every requested dimension simultaneously; never hide one behind a toggle.\r\n\r\n### Maps\r\n\r\n- Let the map dominate the composition. Use at most one compact selection/detail area and only requested controls.\r\n- Always project published GeoJSON/TopoJSON and sourced longitude/latitude with `d3-geo`; never hard-code or hand-draw geographic outlines. Use schematic maps only when asked.\r\n- For world countries, import `https://esm.sh/@d3-maps/atlas@1.0.0/world/countries/countries-110m` and convert it with `topojson-client@3.1.0` using `feature(world, world.objects.features).features`. Join input ISO3 directly to `feature.properties.id`, which is already ISO3; do not convert it to numbers.\r\n- For US states or counties, use `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/us-atlas@3/counties-10m.json/+esm`. For ZIP/ZCTA or city boundaries, download official Census or local open-data GeoJSON; do not guess sibling atlas paths or import raw JSON as JavaScript.\r\n- Keep maps geographically legible: for local points, fetch published neighborhood, street, or comparable geometry; a blank field or lone administrative outline is not a basemap. Show the full city or region behind points or partial choropleths, and frame the locations with modest padding.\r\n- Include the verified geometry in the final HTML. Open it before replying and fix blank basemaps, failed imports, missing labels, or unprojected points.\r\n\r\n### Dense categorical grid\r\n\r\n- Use one compact horizontal selected-item summary, then a grid with exactly one readable identifier per cell, then one small legend. Render only that identifier as visible cell text; put all other metadata in an accessible label or one summary line, not badges or fact grids. Allow only selection unless asked.\r\n\r\n### Part-to-whole or time allocation\r\n\r\n- Use compact metrics and one stacked chart of category allocation per period. Never substitute totals-only bars or duplicate it as a heatmap and totals chart.\r\n\r\n## Layout and accessibility\r\n\r\n- Use semantic HTML, keyboard-accessible controls, and concise labels.\r\n- Use `aria-live=\"polite\"` for dynamic results, selections, and simulator updates. Use `role=\"alert\"` for validation errors. Do not announce every hover or animation frame.\r\n- Keep the top-level surface transparent and unframed, and fill the available conversation width. Design for 736px, or 1,024px in wide mode, and support widths down to 320px. Stack side-by-side content when it no longer fits.\r\n- At every supported width, text, controls, cards, toolbars, and dynamic content must fit without overlap or clipping. Reflow by stacking or wrapping; use `.table-responsive` only when table columns cannot fit. The host sizes the frame to its content, so avoid fixed outer widths, other horizontal overflow, internal scrolling, `position: fixed`, and viewport-height layouts.\r\n- Size every SVG from its actual container. At narrow widths, reduce ticks, declutter annotations, and keep visible text at least 11 screen pixels; never shrink a fixed-width `viewBox`.\r\n- Keep native tab order; never add `tabindex`.\r\n- Use native `button`, `input`, `select`, and `textarea` elements with matching utilities; never recreate controls.\r\n- Keep browser or utility focus styles; never override them.\r\n- On coarse pointers, provide non-overlapping effective targets about 44px by 44px without breaking 320px layouts; visible icons and marks may stay small. Keep fine-pointer controls compact, and let shared utilities own touch sizing and at least 16px editable-field text.\r\n- Keep essential content and actions available without hover.\r\n- Try to keep 90×50px clear for host controls (top-right in LTR hosts, top-left in RTL hosts).\r\n\r\n## Design system\r\n\r\n- Let utilities own geometry, appearance, and interaction. Use the matching utility for every button and form control. Never restyle utilities, descendants, or pseudo-elements: no custom sizes, spacing, borders, radii, shadows, colors, or interaction states.\r\n\r\n### Surfaces and layout\r\n\r\n- `.card`: The only card-like HTML surface. Use its base class unchanged for a necessary numeric summary, selected-item summary, or bounded interactive field. Before adding a fill, border, radius, or shadow to any layout container, either use `.card` or leave it transparent and unframed; never recreate card chrome on rows, panels, tiles, sections, or wrappers. Keep charts, maps, diagrams, tables, controls, and the whole visualization unframed. Never nest cards; show 2-4 summaries near the top only when useful. Structural groupings and repeated content are not bounded interactive fields. Organize them with layout or visual marks, not container chrome.\r\n- `.viz-stat`: Use a summary `.card` with one muted label, one `.viz-stat-value`, and at most one short context or delta line.\r\n- `.viz-grid`: Use for peer metrics or choices instead of a custom grid. It creates as many equal-width columns as fit and stacks when narrow. Never use it for the whole visual or a horizontally scrolling card row. Keep groups to 2-3 columns at 736px and controls in a separate row.\r\n- `.viz-row`: Use as a wrapping horizontal group with centered related values or inline actions that may wrap when narrow.\r\n- `<hr>`: Use a native horizontal rule for a subtle theme-aware separator.\r\n- `.nav.nav-pills` + `.nav-link`: Use the accessible, interactive [Tabs](#tabs) API below.\r\n- `.progress` + `.progress-bar`: `<div class=\"progress\" role=\"progressbar\" aria-label=\"Progress\" aria-valuenow=\"25\" aria-valuemin=\"0\" aria-valuemax=\"100\"><div class=\"progress-bar\" style=\"width:25%\"></div></div>`\r\n- `.viz-tile`: Add to a selectable dense-grid `.btn`; it stretches to fill its grid cell, preserves category fill, and uses an accent ring instead of solid selection. Never add another selected, pressed, border, outline, or shadow rule.\r\n- `.viz-badge`: Use as a compact display-only accent pill for a short status, category, or value; never as a button.\r\n- `.viz-controls`: Use as a wrapping row for controls affecting the same visualization. Keep button groups compact. Put labeled fields directly inside as `.form-label`; fields form at most two columns and stack when narrow.\r\n\r\n### Tabs\r\n\r\n- `.nav.nav-pills[role=\"tablist\"]`: Group content-width native `.nav-link[role=\"tab\"]` buttons and label the group with `aria-label`. Add `.nav-justified` only when tabs should share and fill the row equally.\r\n- `.nav-link[role=\"tab\"]`: Give each button a unique `id`, `type=\"button\"`, `aria-controls`, and `aria-selected`. Mark the initial tab `.active` and `aria-selected=\"true\"`; use `disabled` or `aria-disabled=\"true\"` when needed.\r\n- `[role=\"tabpanel\"]`: Match `id` to its tab's `aria-controls`, set `aria-labelledby` to the tab's `id`, and mark inactive panels `hidden`. Tabs can have separate panels or point to one shared panel.\r\n- Tab behavior is already implemented by the JavaScript runtime and does not need to be wired.\r\n\r\n```html\r\n<div class=\"nav nav-pills\" role=\"tablist\" aria-label=\"Platform\">\r\n <button class=\"nav-link active\" id=\"mac\" role=\"tab\" aria-controls=\"mac-panel\" aria-selected=\"true\" type=\"button\">macOS</button>\r\n <button class=\"nav-link\" id=\"linux\" role=\"tab\" aria-controls=\"linux-panel\" aria-selected=\"false\" type=\"button\">Linux</button>\r\n</div>\r\n<div id=\"mac-panel\" role=\"tabpanel\" aria-labelledby=\"mac\">macOS content</div>\r\n<div id=\"linux-panel\" role=\"tabpanel\" aria-labelledby=\"linux\" hidden>Linux content</div>\r\n```\r\n\r\n### Controls\r\n\r\n- Use `.cursor-interaction` on custom interactive elements, including locally styled widget controls. It follows the host cursor preference; never hardcode `cursor:pointer`. Shared controls already apply it. Preserve text, drag and disabled cursors for those states.\r\n\r\n- Place related inputs and buttons on one row, aligned at their vertical centers. Put labels and values on a separate row above them.\r\n- `.btn`: Use for a content-sized secondary action. Add `.btn-primary` for one main action per control group or `.btn-ghost` for low emphasis.\r\n- `.btn-block`: Add to a `.btn` only when the action should intentionally fill the available inline space. Never use it for ordinary row actions.\r\n- `<a>`: Use for links. Add `.btn` to style a link as a button.\r\n- `[data-tooltip]`: Use for concise supplementary plain text on static or dynamic triggers; the sandbox handles hover, focus, and touch and creates `.tooltip` elements. Keep essential content visible and triggers labeled. Never use `title`, custom markup, or initialization. Example: `<button type=\"button\" data-tooltip=\"Reset view\">Reset</button>`.\r\n- When a visible label is truncated, put its full text in `data-tooltip` on the existing accessible trigger so hover, focus, and tap reveal it. The bundled calendar does this automatically.\r\n- `[data-tooltip-placement]`: Optionally prefer `top` (default), `right`, `bottom`, or `left`; collision handling may flip it.\r\n- `.form-check`: Prefer a wrapping `<label class=\"form-check\">` around the native `.form-check-input` and `.form-check-label` text so the whole row is tappable. An explicit label with matching `for` and input `id` also works.\r\n- `.form-switch`: Add to `.form-check` around a native checkbox.\r\n- `.form-control`: Pair a native text, date, file, or color input—or a textarea—with `.form-label`.\r\n- `.form-control-color`: Add to `.form-control` for a compact native color input.\r\n- `.form-select`: Pair a native select with `.form-label`.\r\n- `.form-range`: Pair a native range with a visible label; put its current value and units immediately before it.\r\n\r\n### Tables\r\n\r\n- `.table`: Use on a semantic table for a quiet, unframed data view. It provides wrapping cells and subtle horizontal dividers without vertical gridlines. Use sentence case for headers.\r\n- `.table-responsive`: Wrap a table when its columns cannot fit at narrow widths. It contains horizontal overflow without clipping the visualization.\r\n- `.table-sm`: Add to `.table` when more rows need to fit; it reduces cell padding without shrinking text.\r\n- `.text-end`, `.text-center`, and `.text-nowrap`: Use inside `.table` for numeric/end alignment, centered values, or values that must stay on one line. Numeric cells use tabular figures when end-aligned.\r\n\r\n### Text\r\n\r\n- `.text-small`: Use for the smallest host-scaled secondary chart labels and annotations, never below 11px or for essential content.\r\n- `.text-muted`: Use for secondary units, captions, timestamps, and context, never essential values or labels.\r\n- `.text-destructive`: Use only for error or validation text the user needs to notice or act on.\r\n- `<code>`: Use for inline commands, file names, symbols, or short references; put multiline code in `<pre><code>`.\r\n- `.sr-only`: Use for visually hidden accessible text.\r\n\r\n## Charts\r\n\r\n- Prefer inline SVG for simple charts and version-pinned approved-CDN libraries when native interaction, scales, legends, or layout materially improve the result.\r\n- Resolve theme colors before passing them to canvas or chart APIs that cannot parse CSS variables or `light-dark(...)`; redraw when the theme changes.\r\n- Use a tooltip unless it would distract from a simple, directly labeled chart. Keep chart-library tooltips and grouped legend interactions native; never replace them with a custom one-point tooltip. For SVG, attach `data-tooltip` directly to the real pointer-accessible mark and include its label, value, and units; the sandbox handles themed positioning, keyboard focus, and touch.\r\n- Animate transitions between chart states so lines and marks move to their new values, resampling paths when point counts differ. Do not animate initial appearance or use fade-only effects; never loop motion, and honor `prefers-reduced-motion`.\r\n- Scope SVG styles to the chart class. Never target every `svg` in a container that also contains Lucide icons.\r\n- Include labeled axes, units, and directly labeled important values. Give every chart, SVG, canvas, and widget a concise screen-reader summary using a role and accessible name or description, SVG `<title>`/`<desc>`, fallback text, or an `.sr-only` heading or description.\r\n- Reserve space for the longest formatted label at every supported width. Axis ticks are secondary and may use `.text-small` when space is tight. Never overlap or clip text against marks, axes, legends, labels, or edges; move or reduce labels rather than squeeze them.\r\n- Add a legend only when multiple series cannot be labeled directly.\r\n- Pair color with shape or text so meaning never depends on color alone.\r\n\r\n## Icons and mockups\r\n\r\n- Use the sandbox-provided global `lucide`. Add an icon name with `data-lucide`:\r\n\r\n ```html\r\n <i data-lucide=\"search\" aria-hidden=\"true\"></i>\r\n ```\r\n\r\n- Never author inline icon SVG or icon paths. Use only supplied Lucide names; the sandbox replaces each placeholder with a host-sized `currentColor` SVG. Reserve authored inline SVG for charts and data marks.\r\n- Mark decorative icons `aria-hidden=\"true\"`. Put action icons inside labeled controls; use a visible label or `aria-label` for icon-only actions.\r\n- Let the sandbox initialize static icons after the fragment without blocking first render. After adding icons dynamically, use `lucide.createIcons({ attrs: { width: 16, height: 16 } })`.\r\n- Never load Lucide or another icon library from the network.\r\n- Use visibly labeled buttons and inputs for small interactions. Keep all presentation-only interaction local to the fragment and make the first render useful before input changes.\r\n- Use semantic controls, realistic spacing, and restrained chrome for mockups. Never fake product screenshots when inspectable UI is needed.\r\n"}"}, {"type": "input_text", "text": "[{"name":"mcp__codex_apps__chatgpt_space_search_sharing_recipients","description":"Read, search, create, and edit pages and spaces in ChatGPT Space, within your cu"},{"name":"mcp__codex_apps__plugin_management_search_plugins","description":"Manage plugins, settings, permissions, and connections. 						79 text 适配快捷卡片
					80 container
						81 text 为了方便用户在使用米家 App、小爱带屏音箱、小米手机负一屏快捷操作和小米电视通过快捷卡片快速控制产品，小米 IoT 平台开放了米家 App 快捷功能，其中包含快捷卡片、耗材信息和环境信息；开发者在小米 IoT 开发者平台上按照小米 IoT 设备协议规范中的内容，使用标准功能定义产品功能后，米家 App 即可 自动适配 产品所需使用的快捷功能。

Keep the `data-chart-hover-guide` at the exact cursor x, interpolate every visible series there, and show one aligned `data-chart-hover-marker` and tooltip row per visible series; never snap the guide to a nearby sample. Never add a KPI row, controls, cards, or panels unless those UI elements are explicitly requested. - For sequences or parallel work, use aligned lanes on one time axis. Encode phase and resource in the marks; annotate totals, waits, and bottlenecks on the axis or lanes, not above the plot. - For distributions or multi-metric comparisons, use shared-scale facets or small multiples. Render every requested dimension simultaneously; never hide one behind a toggle. ### Maps - Let the map dominate the composition. Use at most one compact selection/detail area and only requested controls. - Always project published GeoJSON/TopoJSON and sourced longitude/latitude with `d3-geo`; never hard-code or hand-draw geographic outlines. Use schematic maps only when asked. - For world countries, import `https://esm.sh/@d3-maps/atlas@1.0.0/world/countries/countries-110m` and convert it with `topojson-client@3.1.0` using `feature(world, world.objects.features).features`. Show the full city or region behind points or partial choropleths, and frame the locations with modest padding. - Include the verified geometry in the final HTML. Open it before replying and fix blank basemaps, failed imports, missing labels, or unprojected points. ### Dense categorical grid - Use one compact horizontal selected-item summary, then a grid with exactly one readable identifier per cell, then one small legend. Render only that identifier as visible cell text; put all other metadata in an accessible label or one summary line, not badges or fact grids. Allow only selection unless asked. ### Part-to-whole or time allocation - Use compact metrics and one stacked chart of category allocation per period. Never substitute totals-only bars or duplicate it as a heatmap and totals chart. ## Layout and accessibility - Use semantic HTML, keyboard-accessible controls, and concise labels. - Use `aria-live="polite"` for dynamic results, selections, and simulator updates. Use `role="alert"` for validation errors. Do not announce every hover or animation frame. - Keep the top-level surface transparent and unframed, and fill the available conversation width. Design for 736px, or 1,024px in wide mode, and support widths down to 320px. Stack side-by-side content when it no longer fits. - At every supported width, text, controls, cards, toolbars, and dynamic content must fit without overlap or clipping. Reflow by stacking or wrapping; use `.table-responsive` only when table columns cannot fit. The host sizes the frame to its content, so avoid fixed outer widths, other horizontal overflow, internal scrolling, `position: fixed`, and viewport-height layouts. - Size every SVG from its actual container. At narrow widths, reduce ticks, declutter annotations, and keep visible text at least 11 screen pixels; never shrink a fixed-width `viewBox`. - Keep native tab order; never add `tabindex`. - Use native `button`, `input`, `select`, and `textarea` elements with matching utilities; never recreate controls. - Keep browser or utility focus styles; never override them. - On coarse pointers, provide non-overlapping effective targets about 44px by 44px without breaking 320px layouts; visible icons and marks may stay small. Keep fine-pointer controls compact, and let shared utilities own touch sizing and at least 16px editable-field text. - Keep essential content and actions available without hover. - Try to keep 90×50px clear for host controls (top-right in LTR hosts, top-left in RTL hosts). ## Design system - Let utilities own geometry, appearance, and interaction. Use the matching utility for every button and form control. Never restyle utilities, descendants, or pseudo-elements: no custom sizes, spacing, borders, radii, shadows, colors, or interaction states. ### Surfaces and layout - `.card`: The only card-like HTML surface. Use its base class unchanged for a necessary numeric summary, selected-item summary, or bounded interactive field. Before adding a fill, border, radius, or shadow to any layout container, either use `.card` or leave it transparent and unframed; never recreate card chrome on rows, panels, tiles, sections, or wrappers. Keep charts, maps, diagrams, tables, controls, and the whole visualization unframed. Never nest cards; show 2-4 summaries near the top only when useful. Structural groupings and repeated content are not bounded interactive fields. Put labels and values on a separate row above them. - `.btn`: Use for a content-sized secondary action. Add `.btn-primary` for one main action per control group or `.btn-ghost` for low emphasis. - `.btn-block`: Add to a `.btn` only when the action should intentionally fill the available inline space. Never use it for ordinary row actions. - `<a>`: Use for links. Put live values in control headers or on the visual before cards. Treat maxima as ceilings, not targets. Both fields accept JSON or `null` and may be omitted (treated as `null`). Each call replaces the snapshot; keep it under 16 KiB. Never save on load or state events.\r\n- Put choices useful for follow-up questions in `modelContent`, UI details worth restoring in `privateContent`, and transient or recomputable values in memory. Only `modelContent` may reach the model: delivery is best-effort and not guaranteed across clients. Never rely on it; saving never starts a turn. No secrets or images.\r\n\r\n### UI mockups\r\n\r\n- For alternative designs of the same component or screen, read [Variant carousel](tweak.md#variant-carousel), even when design controls are not requested. Use descriptive variant names without numeric or ordinal prefixes (for example, `Compact`, never `01 · Compact`); the carousel already displays the count.\r\n- Include a few thoughtfully chosen design alternatives whenever they would help the user explore a mockup, without waiting for the user to ask. Read [tweak.md](tweak.md) and bind useful options with the host-provided `Tweak` helper. Keep ordinary mockup interactions local; do not add design controls to charts, explainers, or simulations unless requested. Do not render a second controls panel or open annotation mode automatically.\r\n- \"In the widget\" means the in-conversation visualization, not a widget inside the depicted product.\r\n- Use product and platform context already available in the conversation; don't search the project to render a mockup. Match the product's chrome, navigation, typography, colors, and content. If its design is unavailable, infer one from the platform and request.\r\n- NEVER use visualization CSS variables or utility classes inside a mockup (for example, `--card`, `--font-size-base`, `.card`, or `.btn`). Define root-scoped, product-specific colors, typography, surfaces, and controls instead. This rule overrides all general visualization guidance.\r\n- Keep only the surrounding conversation surface transparent. Give product windows, cards, menus, and popovers opaque backgrounds, and stack overlays above the product content.\r\n- Follow the host's active appearance with product-specific `light-dark(<light>, <dark>)` colors unless a fixed theme is requested.\r\n- **Contained mockup:** Frame a component, dialog, small feature, or mobile screen as a compact product surface. Add `.viz-dotted-background` to the surrounding preview area or carousel root for a quiet, theme-aware dot grid. This preview-only class is an exception to the mockup utility rule; keep it outside the product UI and leave full-page mockups, charts, and explainers plain.\r\n- **Full-page mockup:** Render a desktop window, application shell, or page at full width without an additional visualization card.\r\n- Put app-wide navigation and pickers in the app chrome, and local controls in their component. Omit single-option pickers. Show realistic states, not invented dashboards, filler cards, or oversized icons.\r\n\r\n### Calendar\r\n\r\n- Use the bundled compact `<viz-calendar>` for a day schedule. Read [Calendar](widgets/calendar.md) and start from the [example](examples/calendar.html). Supply verified dates and events; the component handles durations, overlap lanes, and responsive layout. Short blocks show the title; hover, focus, or tap reveals the full title, time, and detail. Do not stretch the schedule to fit secondary text or wrap the element in another card.\r\n\r\n### Interactive explainer or simulation\r\n\r\n- Use compact controls or status, one compact dominant visual, and at most one single-line selected-state detail. Default to no summary cards; allow up to three only when changing metrics are central.\r\n- Crop empty space and fit the available inline width. For step-throughs, add only requested step controls and update one current visual; never add parameter controls, formulas, metric cards, or side-by-side steps unless asked.\r\n\r\n### Graphs and plots\r\n\r\n- Use D3 for data-rich Cartesian or statistical plots and handwritten SVG for simple, directly labeled values. Keep diagrams, simulations, and maps under their existing guidance. Load the version-pinned approved-CDN script `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/d3@7.9.0/dist/d3.min.js`.\r\n- Render the figure, legend, and subplots directly on the transparent host surface. Frame only the SVG plot area; never wrap charts in `.card`, rounded panels, filled backgrounds, or shadowed containers.\r\n- Give the figure a concise visible title. Render each Cartesian subplot in its own responsive SVG with a matching `viewBox`, a thin frame, and visible `text.axis-title[data-axis=\"x\"]` and `text.axis-title[data-axis=\"y\"]` showing quantities and units.\r\n- Set each SVG `viewBox` from its own container's measured width, redraw with `ResizeObserver`, and reserve at least 64px for the y axis. Never scale down a fixed-width `viewBox`.\r\n- Derive padded domains with `d3.extent(...)` over all observations, uncertainty, and references. Inset scale ranges for marker radii and keep every path inside `rect[data-chart-frame]`; never draw endpoint connectors outside the frame or guess or hard-code the domain.\r\n- After every draw, measure tick, axis, and value-label bounds together. Leave 4px between labels, anchor edge labels inward, and remove optional annotations first. At 360px, show at most four x ticks and stack panels.\r\n- Prefer `--viz-series-1` through `--viz-series-6` for chart series; use `--foreground` and `--border` for neutrals, cycle the six series tokens when more are needed, and never use literal or fallback colors. Give every SVG label `fill: var(--foreground)` and `font-size: 12px`; never shrink labels below 11 screen pixels. Stack subplots when their labels no longer fit.\r\n- Keep observations, trends, and important values visible. Use bands for dense uncertainty, whiskers for isolated estimates, and one compact, wrapping legend. Render one real `<button type=\"button\" aria-pressed=\"true\">` per series with a small swatch and neutral text; toggle its line, markers, and tooltip row together. Keep buttons transparent, borderless, and indistinguishable from inline text; never use `.btn`, pills, badges, rounded borders, or filled and selected backgrounds.\r\n- Share one root-relative, pointer-transparent `<div class=\"tooltip\" role=\"tooltip\">` using `--popover` and `--popover-foreground`. In each multi-series SVG, give the full-plot overlay both `data-chart-hit` and `data-chart-hover-overlay=\"cross-series\"`. Keep the `data-chart-hover-guide` at the exact cursor x, interpolate every visible series there, and show one aligned `data-chart-hover-marker` and tooltip row per visible series; never snap the guide to a nearby sample. Let touch users pin the same cross-series details without requiring hover.\r\n- Find ordered observations with `d3.bisector(d => d.x).center(values, x)`; never pass an accessor to `d3.bisectCenter`.\r\n- Give isolated marks transparent `data-chart-hit` targets at least 32 screen pixels across on fine pointers and about 44px on coarse pointers; use one nearest-point overlay for dense scatter.\r\n- For named numeric data and one-off analyses, start with the plot. Put values and takeaways on its marks, axes, or annotations. Never add a KPI row, controls, cards, or panels unless those UI elements are explicitly requested.\r\n- For sequences or parallel work, use aligned lanes on one time axis. Encode phase and resource in the marks; annotate totals, waits, and bottlenecks on the axis or lanes, not above the plot.\r\n- For distributions or multi-metric comparisons, use shared-scale facets or small multiples. Render every requested dimension simultaneously; never hide one behind a toggle.\r\n\r\n### Maps\r\n\r\n- Let the map dominate the composition. Use at most one compact selection/detail area and only requested controls.\r\n- Always project published GeoJSON/TopoJSON and sourced longitude/latitude with `d3-geo`; never hard-code or hand-draw geographic outlines. Use schematic maps only when asked.\r\n- For world countries, import `https://esm.sh/@d3-maps/atlas@1.0.0/world/countries/countries-110m` and convert it with `topojson-client@3.1.0` using `feature(world, world.objects.features).features`. Join input ISO3 directly to `feature.properties.id`, which is already ISO3; do not convert it to numbers.\r\n- For US states or counties, use `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/us-atlas@3/counties-10m.json/+esm`. For ZIP/ZCTA or city boundaries, download official Census or local open-data GeoJSON; do not guess sibling atlas paths or import raw JSON as JavaScript.\r\n- Keep maps geographically legible: for local points, fetch published neighborhood, street, or comparable geometry; a blank field or lone administrative outline is not a basemap. Show the full city or region behind points or partial choropleths, and frame the locations with modest padding.\r\n- Include the verified geometry in the final HTML. Open it before replying and fix blank basemaps, failed imports, missing labels, or unprojected points.\r\n\r\n### Dense categorical grid\r\n\r\n- Use one compact horizontal selected-item summary, then a grid with exactly one readable identifier per cell, then one small legend. Render only that identifier as visible cell text; put all other metadata in an accessible label or one summary line, not badges or fact grids. Allow only selection unless asked.\r\n\r\n### Part-to-whole or time allocation\r\n\r\n- Use compact metrics and one stacked chart of category allocation per period. Never substitute totals-only bars or duplicate it as a heatmap and totals chart.\r\n\r\n## Layout and accessibility\r\n\r\n- Use semantic HTML, keyboard-accessible controls, and concise labels.\r\n- Use `aria-live=\"polite\"` for dynamic results, selections, and simulator updates. Use `role=\"alert\"` for validation errors. Do not announce every hover or animation frame.\r\n- Keep the top-level surface transparent and unframed, and fill the available conversation width. Design for 736px, or 1,024px in wide mode, and support widths down to 320px. Stack side-by-side content when it no longer fits.\r\n- At every supported width, text, controls, cards, toolbars, and dynamic content must fit without overlap or clipping. Reflow by stacking or wrapping; use `.table-responsive` only when table columns cannot fit. The host sizes the frame to its content, so avoid fixed outer widths, other horizontal overflow, internal scrolling, `position: fixed`, and viewport-height layouts.\r\n- Size every SVG from its actual container. At narrow widths, reduce ticks, declutter annotations, and keep visible text at least 11 screen pixels; never shrink a fixed-width `viewBox`.\r\n- Keep native tab order; never add `tabindex`.\r\n- Use native `button`, `input`, `select`, and `textarea` elements with matching utilities; never recreate controls.\r\n- Keep browser or utility focus styles; never override them.\r\n- On coarse pointers, provide non-overlapping effective targets about 44px by 44px without breaking 320px layouts; visible icons and marks may stay small. Keep fine-pointer controls compact, and let shared utilities own touch sizing and at least 16px editable-field text.\r\n- Keep essential content and actions available without hover.\r\n- Try to keep 90×50px clear for host controls (top-right in LTR hosts, top-left in RTL hosts).\r\n\r\n## Design system\r\n\r\n- Let utilities own geometry, appearance, and interaction. Use the matching utility for every button and form control. Never restyle utilities, descendants, or pseudo-elements: no custom sizes, spacing, borders, radii, shadows, colors, or interaction states.\r\n\r\n### Surfaces and layout\r\n\r\n- `.card`: The only card-like HTML surface. Use its base class unchanged for a necessary numeric summary, selected-item summary, or bounded interactive field. Before adding a fill, border, radius, or shadow to any layout container, either use `.card` or leave it transparent and unframed; never recreate card chrome on rows, panels, tiles, sections, or wrappers. Keep charts, maps, diagrams, tables, controls, and the whole visualization unframed. Never nest cards; show 2-4 summaries near the top only when useful. Structural groupings and repeated content are not bounded interactive fields. Organize them with layout or visual marks, not container chrome.\r\n- `.viz-stat`: Use a summary `.card` with one muted label, one `.viz-stat-value`, and at most one short context or delta line.\r\n- `.viz-grid`: Use for peer metrics or choices instead of a custom grid. It creates as many equal-width columns as fit and stacks when narrow. Never use it for the whole visual or a horizontally scrolling card row. Keep groups to 2-3 columns at 736px and controls in a separate row.\r\n- `.viz-row`: Use as a wrapping horizontal group with centered related values or inline actions that may wrap when narrow.\r\n- `<hr>`: Use a native horizontal rule for a subtle theme-aware separator.\r\n- `.nav.nav-pills` + `.nav-link`: Use the accessible, interactive [Tabs](#tabs) API below.\r\n- `.progress` + `.progress-bar`: `<div class=\"progress\" role=\"progressbar\" aria-label=\"Progress\" aria-valuenow=\"25\" aria-valuemin=\"0\" aria-valuemax=\"100\"><div class=\"progress-bar\" style=\"width:25%\"></div></div>`\r\n- `.viz-tile`: Add to a selectable dense-grid `.btn`; it stretches to fill its grid cell, preserves category fill, and uses an accent ring instead of solid selection. Put labeled fields directly inside as `.form-label`; fields form at most two columns and stack when narrow.\r\n\r\n### Tabs\r\n\r\n- `.nav.nav-pills[role=\"tablist\"]`: Group content-width native `.nav-link[role=\"tab\"]` buttons and label the group with `aria-label`. Add `.btn` to style a link as a button.\r\n- `[data-tooltip]`: Use for concise supplementary plain text on static or dynamic triggers; the sandbox handles hover, focus, and touch and creates `.tooltip` elements. Example: `<button type=\"button\" data-tooltip=\"Reset view\">Reset</button>`.\r\n- When a visible label is truncated, put its full text in `data-tooltip` on the existing accessible trigger so hover, focus, and tap reveal it. It provides wrapping cells and subtle horizontal dividers without vertical gridlines. Use sentence case for headers.\r\n- `.table-responsive`: Wrap a table when its columns cannot fit at narrow widths. It contains horizontal overflow without clipping the visualization.\r\n- `.table-sm`: Add to `.table` when more rows need to fit; it reduces cell padding without shrinking text.\r\n- `.text-end`, `.text-center`, and `.text-nowrap`: Use inside `.table` for numeric/end alignment, centered values, or values that must stay on one line. Keep chart-library tooltips and grouped legend interactions native; never replace them with a custom one-point tooltip. For SVG, attach `data-tooltip` directly to the real pointer-accessible mark and include its label, value, and units; the sandbox handles themed positioning, keyboard focus, and touch.\r\n- Animate transitions between chart states so lines and marks move to their new values, resampling paths when point counts differ. Do not animate initial appearance or use fade-only effects; never loop motion, and honor `prefers-reduced-motion`.\r\n- Scope SVG styles to the chart class. Never target every `svg` in a container that also contains Lucide icons.\r\n- Include labeled axes, units, and directly labeled important values. Axis ticks are secondary and may use `.text-small` when space is tight. Never overlap or clip text against marks, axes, legends, labels, or edges; move or reduce labels rather than squeeze them.\r\n- Add a legend only when multiple series cannot be labeled directly.\r\n- Pair color with shape or text so meaning never depends on color alone.\r\n\r\n## Icons and mockups\r\n\r\n- Use the sandbox-provided global `lucide`. Add an icon name with `data-lucide`:\r\n\r\n ```html\r\n <i data-lucide=\"search\" aria-hidden=\"true\"></i>\r\n ```\r\n\r\n- Never author inline icon SVG or icon paths. Use only supplied Lucide names; the sandbox replaces each placeholder with a host-sized `currentColor` SVG. Reserve authored inline SVG for charts and data marks.\r\n- Mark decorative icons `aria-hidden=\"true\"`. Put action icons inside labeled controls; use a visible label or `aria-label` for icon-only actions.\r\n- Let the sandbox initialize static icons after the fragment without blocking first render. After adding icons dynamically, use `lucide.createIcons({ attrs: { width: 16, height: 16 } })`.\r\n- Never load Lucide or another icon library from the network.\r\n- Use visibly labeled buttons and inputs for small interactions. Keep all presentation-only interaction local to the fragment and make the first render useful before input changes.\r\n- Use semantic controls, realistic spacing, and restrained chrome for mockups. Never fake product screenshots when inspectable UI is needed.\r\n\r\n"}"}]}
